DT-MRI provides quantitative measures that reflect the severity of neuropsychological deficits in patients with MS.

the relationship between the cognitive dysfunction and brain damage in patients with RR-MS.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DT-MRI provides metrics that are more sensitive to the microscopic aspects of the MS lesions than conventional imaging.
DT-MRI is a useful tool to assess the macroscopic and microscopic lesions and the NAWM/NAGM damage in RRMS patients, and that these lesions and damage are correlated with cognitive deficits.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cognitive dysfunction in patients with RR MS is correlated with DT-MR imaging metrics, and that these metrics reflect both the extent and the severity of the macroscopic and microscopic damage of the NABT.
cognitive dysfunction in patients with RR multiple sclerosis is correlated with both the macroscopic lesion load and with the microscopic damage of the brain tissue.
DT-MRI may be a useful tool to assess the severity of the cognitive impairment in MS patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extent of the macroscopic lesion load and the extent of damage to the NAWM are both associated with cognitive dysfunction.
cognitive impairment in MS is a multifactorial process that is not only dependent on the macroscopic lesion load.
